en: to associate A with B; to link in one's mind

examples.en: If you link words with pictures, they're easy to memorize.
I associate that song with summer.
There's no evidence to link the two incidents.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 돈과 연관시키는 사람이 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like people who connect everything to money.
The teacher tied what we learned to everyday life.
Don't force a connection; just state the facts.

explain: 스스로 이어진 건 '연관되다', 누군가가 이은 건 '연관시키다'로 구분해요. '~을/를 ~와 연관시키다' 구조라서 목적어가 꼭 따라와요. 사람이 두 가지를 생각이나 행동으로 이어 놓을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 이 냄새를 어릴 때 기억과 연관시켜 생각해요.
phrases.en: I link this smell with childhood memories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관시키다'를 '-아/어서 생각하다'와 연결해 마음속으로 잇는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing it with 생각하다 makes clear the link is made in the mind.
phrases.en_equiv: to think of in connection with

phrases.en: Please don't link me with that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘을 이어서 보지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to connect two things together.

phrases.en: Try connecting this word with a picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관시키다'보다 쉬운 말이고, 눈에 보이는 것을 잇는 데도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that can also be used for physically linking things.

explain_en: Someone connects A to B, takes object (바다와 연관시키다) Things that connect by themselves are '연관되다'; when someone connects them, it is '연관시키다'. The structure is '~을/를 ~와 연관시키다', so it always takes an object. Use it when a person links two things in thought or action.

dis.h: make a link: associate A with B
gh: formal: tie A firmly to B

p.n: 결부시키다 is more formal and stresses tying A firmly to B.

en: to be eternal; to be everlasting

examples.en: I wish love were everlasting.
Nothing in the world is eternal.
I hope our friendship lasts forever.
That song is eternal in my heart.
Happiness is not forever, but it is precious.
I want to be friends forever.

explain: '영원하다'는 끝이 없다는 느낌으로 노래, 영화, 편지 속 말에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '평생', '언제까지나'가 더 자주 들려요. 부사는 '영원히'예요: '영원히 잊지 않을게요'.

phrases.en: The movie talks about eternal love.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영원하다'를 꾸밈말로 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing using '영원하다' as a modifier.

phrases.en: Good times don't last forever.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 있다는 뜻으로 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it will end someday.

phrases.en: I hope our friendship lasts forever.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소원이나 편지에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in wishes and letters.

explain_en: 영원하다 has a feeling of no end and often appears in songs, movies and letters. In daily talk, 평생 or 언제까지나 are heard more often. The adverb is 영원히, as in '영원히 잊지 않을게요'.

examples.ko: 제 인생철학은 하루하루 최선을 다하는 거예요.
examples.en: My philosophy of life is to do my best every single day.
I want to learn my grandfather's philosophy of life.

examples.ko: 그 책에는 작가의 인생철학이 잘 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The author's philosophy of life comes through well in that book.

examples.ko: 인생철학이 뚜렷한 사람은 쉽게 흔들리지 않아요.
examples.en: People with a clear philosophy of life aren't easily shaken.

examples.ko: 면접에서 자신의 인생철학을 말해 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: In the interview, they asked me to talk about my philosophy of life.
My philosophy of life changed while I was traveling.

explain: 학문으로서의 철학이 아니라 개인이 삶에서 지키는 생각이나 원칙을 말해요. '가치관'과 비슷하지만 '인생철학'은 한마디로 말할 수 있는 신조 같은 느낌이 있어요. '제 인생철학은 ~예요'처럼 자기소개나 인터뷰에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I have my own philosophy of life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기만의 신조를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about your own personal principle.

phrases.en: His philosophy of life is firm, so he doesn't waver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각과 원칙이 분명한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person whose thoughts and principles are clear.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a firm philosophy of life

phrases.example: 제 가치관은 정직이 가장 중요하다는 거예요.
phrases.en: My values are that honesty is the most important.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 '가치관'은 한마디 신조보다 생각의 기준 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, but 가치관 refers to one's whole set of standards rather than a one-line creed.

explain_en: It is not philosophy as an academic field but the personal ideas or principles a person lives by. It is close to '가치관', though '인생철학' feels more like a motto you can sum up in one line. You often hear '제 인생철학은 ~예요' in introductions and interviews.

examples.en: I attached a tag with my name on it to my bag.

examples.ko: 새 옷의 꼬리표에 가격이 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The price is written on the tag of the new clothes.

examples.ko: 한 번 붙은 꼬리표는 쉽게 떨어지지 않아요.
examples.en: Once a label is stuck on, it does not come off easily.
He had a hard time because of the 'troublemaker' label.

examples.ko: 택배 상자마다 번호가 있는 꼬리표가 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: Every delivery box had a tag with a number on it.

examples.ko: 꼬리표 없는 가방은 주인을 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: A bag without a tag is hard to return to its owner.

explain: '이름표'는 이름을 적어 단 표이고, 꼬리표는 짐이나 상품에 다는 작은 표예요. 사람에게 '꼬리표가 붙다'라고 하면 '문제아' 같은 이미지가 계속 따라다녀요. 그래서 좋은 말보다는 나쁜 평가에 더 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 한 번 실수하면 꼬리표가 붙어서 오래가요.
phrases.en: to get labeled
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 어떤 평가나 이미지가 굳어져 따라다닌다는 비유예요. 주로 부정적인 이미지에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech meaning an evaluation or image sticks to a person. Mostly used for negative images.

explain_en: A tag or label attached to things; also figurative stigma. An 이름표 shows a name, while a 꼬리표 is a small tag attached to luggage or goods. When a 꼬리표 sticks to a person, an image like 문제아 follows them around. It is used more for bad labels than for good ones.

t90.ax: I attached a tag with my name on it to the bag.

examples.en: The computer tower is too hot.
I connected the main unit and the monitor with a cable.

examples.ko: 새 본체를 사려고 전자 상가에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the electronics market to buy a new tower.
When the mask came off, the monster's true form was revealed.
I carried the vacuum cleaner's main body up the stairs.
The power button is on the back of the main unit.

explain: 본체는 부품이나 부속품을 뺀 기계의 몸통 부분이에요. 컴퓨터에서는 모니터·키보드를 뺀 박스를 '본체'라고 해서 일상에서 아주 자주 써요. 이야기 속에서는 가짜 모습을 벗은 진짜 모습도 '본체'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put the computer tower under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모니터와 키보드를 뺀 컴퓨터 박스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The computer box itself, without the monitor and keyboard.

phrases.en: Please press the power button on the main unit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계의 몸통 부분에 있는 전원을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The power on the main body of a machine.

phrases.en: At the end of the story, the monster revealed its true form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기 속에서 가짜 모습을 벗고 진짜 모습을 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in stories when a character shows its real form.

explain_en: The real entity or thing behind a disguise; not about feelings. 본체 is the main body of a machine without its parts and accessories. For computers, the box without the monitor and keyboard is called 본체, which is very common in daily life. In stories, the real form under a disguise is also called 본체.

examples.en: Someone is banging on the door.
I was startled by the crash of thunder.

examples.ko: 위층에서 쾅쾅 소리가 나서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: There were loud thumps from upstairs, so I couldn't sleep.
He got angry and pounded the desk.
They are hammering away with an iron hammer at the construction site.

examples.ko: 문을 쾅쾅 닫지 말고 살살 닫아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't slam the door; close it gently.

explain: 크고 단단한 것이 세게 부딪히거나 두드리는 소리예요. 작고 가벼운 소리는 '콩콩'이에요. 문을 '쾅쾅 두드리다'는 급하거나 화난 느낌이라, 보통 노크는 '똑똑'이 어울려요.

phrases.example: 화가 난 동생이 문을 쾅쾅 닫고 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: My angry younger sibling went in, slamming the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 닫아서 큰 소리가 날 때 써요. 화난 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a door is shut hard with a loud noise, often suggesting anger.

phrases.example: 밖에서 쾅쾅 소리가 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I was startled by a thumping noise from outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소리'를 붙여 명사처럼 쓰고, 크고 단단한 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '소리' makes it noun-like, for loud, hard sounds.

phrases.example: 공사 소리가 쾅쾅 울려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: The construction noise boomed, so I couldn't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 소리가 주변에 크게 퍼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a loud sound resonates through the surroundings.

explain_en: It is the sound of something big and hard hitting or being struck hard. The small, light version is '콩콩'. Knocking '쾅쾅' on a door feels urgent or angry, so for a normal knock '똑똑' fits better.

t90.ax: Someone is banging on the door.

examples.ko: 오래 써서 톱의 톱니가 많이 닳았어요.
examples.en: The teeth of the saw have worn down from long use.

examples.ko: 시계 안에는 작은 톱니가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: There are lots of tiny gear teeth inside a watch.

examples.ko: 오래 써서 톱을 바꿨어요. 톱니가 다 닳았거든요.
examples.en: I replaced the saw because its teeth were all worn down.
Try cutting the paper into a zigzag shape.
The two gears mesh and the machine runs.
The bicycle chain came off the sprocket.

examples.ko: 이 빵칼은 톱니가 있어서 부드러운 빵도 잘 잘려요.
examples.en: This bread knife has serrations, so it cuts soft bread well.

explain: 톱니는 톱뿐 아니라 기계 바퀴(기어)의 이에도 써요. 가장자리가 톱처럼 울퉁불퉁한 모양을 말할 때는 '톱니 모양'이라고 해요. 사람 이는 '이빨'이나 '치아'라고 해서 말이 달라요.

phrases.en: The gears turn and the clock moves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 톱니가 있는 바퀴 전체를 말해요. '톱니'는 그 이 하나하나예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The whole wheel with teeth; '톱니' is each tooth on it.

phrases.en: The edge of this snack has a saw-tooth shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 아니라 울퉁불퉁한 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a jagged shape, not for machines.

phrases.example: 톱니가 닳아서 톱이 잘 안 잘려요.
phrases.en: The teeth are worn down, so the saw doesn't cut well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 써서 톱니가 무뎌졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the teeth have gone dull from long use.

explain_en: 톱니 covers both saw teeth and the teeth of a gear wheel. A zigzag edge is called '톱니 모양'. For people's teeth you say '이빨' or '치아' instead.

en: wedding goods; items prepared for marriage

examples.ko: 결혼 전에 혼수품을 사러 가구점에 갔어요.
examples.en: Before the wedding, I went to a furniture store to buy items for the new home.

examples.ko: 혼수품 때문에 두 집안이 의견이 달랐어요.
examples.en: The two families disagreed over the wedding household items.
The bride's mother wrote down a list of wedding items.

examples.ko: 요즘은 혼수품을 간단하게 준비하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people prepare wedding household items simply.
We bought a refrigerator and a washing machine as wedding household items.

examples.ko: 혼수품은 신혼집에 맞춰서 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to choose wedding household items to fit the newlyweds' home.

explain: 결혼할 때 새 살림을 위해 마련하는 가구, 가전, 옷, 이불 같은 물건을 말해요. 줄여서 '혼수'라고도 하고, '혼수를 준비하다', '혼수를 해 가다'처럼 써요. 결혼 이야기에서 가끔 부담스러운 주제로 나오기도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm busy these days because of the wedding goods.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼수품'을 줄인 말로 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form used more often in conversation.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 같이 혼수를 준비하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two of them are preparing wedding goods together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼 전에 물건을 마련할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for getting things ready before a wedding.

phrases.en: I wrote down a list of wedding items.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 살지 정리할 때 '목록'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'list' when organizing what to buy.

explain_en: It refers to furniture, appliances, clothes, bedding, and other things prepared for a new household at marriage. It is often shortened to '혼수', as in '혼수를 준비하다'. In talk about weddings it can sometimes be a touchy topic because of the cost.

examples.en: The company made Busan its logistics hub.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 우리의 해외 진출 거점이에요.
examples.en: This city is our base for overseas expansion.

examples.ko: 등산할 때 이 산장을 거점으로 쓰면 편해요.
examples.en: When hiking, it's convenient to use this lodge as a base.

examples.ko: 새로운 거점을 만들려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Creating a new base costs a lot of money.
I was treated at a regional hub hospital.

examples.ko: 거점이 있어야 사업을 넓힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need a base to expand your business.

explain: 어떤 활동을 하기 위해 중심이 되는 장소를 말해요. '본사'나 '집'처럼 원래 있는 곳이 아니라, 일을 넓히거나 이동하기 위해 잡아 두는 곳이에요. '물류 거점', '활동 거점', '거점 병원'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The company set up a base overseas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 활동의 중심이 될 곳을 새로 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means setting up a new place to be the center of activity.

phrases.example: 이 동네가 우리 모임의 활동 거점이에요.
phrases.en: This neighborhood is the base of our group's activities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이나 단체가 주로 움직이는 중심 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The main place from which a group or organization operates.

phrases.en: Daejeon is a hub city for transportation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 활동이나 교통의 중심이 되는 도시를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A city that is the center of many activities or of transportation.

explain_en: A physical or strategic base for activity, such as a city or facility. A place that serves as the center for some activity. It isn't a head office or home, but a spot you set up to expand work or move around from. It often comes before other nouns, as in 물류 거점 (logistics hub), 활동 거점 and 거점 병원 (regional hub hospital).

t90.ax: You need a base to expand your business.

examples.en: My younger sibling guessed my password as if by magic.
Mom spots a lie in no time, like she has a sixth sense.
He shows up out of nowhere only when I'm hungry.
He solved the problem with uncanny speed.

examples.ko: 제가 지갑을 두고 온 걸 귀신같이 아셨네요.
examples.en: You figured out uncannily that I left my wallet behind.
My older brother found my weak spot uncannily fast.

explain: 귀신처럼 정확하고 빠르게 무언가를 알거나 해내는 모습을 말해요. '귀신같이 알다', '귀신같이 맞히다', '귀신같이 나타나다'를 자주 써요. 감탄이나 가벼운 놀림이 섞인 구어체예요.

phrases.en: Mom finds even hidden things as if by magic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾기 어려운 것을 아주 빨리 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone finds something hard to find very quickly.

phrases.en: A friend showed up uncannily just when I was hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱 맞는 때에 나타난 것이 신기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone appears at just the right moment.

phrases.en: That person is uncannily perceptive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀신같이'의 기본형인 형용사로, 사람의 능력을 칭찬하거나 놀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective that 귀신같이 comes from, used to praise or tease someone's ability.

explain_en: It describes knowing or doing something with uncanny accuracy and speed. Common pairings are '귀신같이 알다', '귀신같이 맞히다' and '귀신같이 나타나다'. It's colloquial, mixing admiration or light teasing.

examples.en: I collected only the egg yolks and made a sauce.

examples.ko: 프라이는 달걀노른자가 안 터지게 구워 주세요.
examples.en: Please fry the egg so the yolk doesn't break.
Egg yolks contain a lot of nutrients.

examples.ko: 케이크를 만들 때 달걀노른자와 흰자를 나눠요.
examples.en: When making a cake, you separate the yolk from the white.
I popped the egg yolk with my chopsticks.
I don't like yolks, so I eat only the whites.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 그냥 '노른자'라고 해요. 반대는 '흰자'(달걀흰자)이고, '달걀' 대신 '계란'이라고도 많이 말해요. 그래서 '계란노른자'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Please set the yolk aside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '달걀'을 빼고 이렇게 짧게 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech people usually drop 'dalgyal' and say just this.

phrases.en: Adding the egg yolk makes it richer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달걀' 대신 '계란'을 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This uses 'gyeran' in place of 'dalgyal'.

phrases.en: Please beat the egg yolk in the bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a common phrase in cooking.

explain_en: In speech people shorten it to just '노른자'. The opposite is '흰자' (달걀흰자), and many people say '계란' instead of '달걀', so you also hear '계란노른자'.

en: to stammer; to stutter; to falter

examples.en: I was so nervous that I stammered.
The child said his name haltingly.
I keep stumbling over my words when I present in a foreign language.

examples.ko: 그는 거짓말이 들킬까 봐 떠듬거리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: He began to stammer, afraid his lie would be found out.

examples.ko: 떠듬거리지 말고 천천히 다시 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't stammer; try saying it again slowly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 떠듬거리는 손자의 말을 끝까지 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother listened to her grandson's halting words until the end.

explain: 말이 매끄럽게 나오지 않고 자꾸 끊기거나 막힐 때 써요. 긴장, 당황, 서툰 외국어처럼 일시적인 이유로 그럴 때 어울려요. 비슷한 '더듬거리다'나 '말을 더듬다'도 같이 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: He apologized, stammering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 말하는 모습을 함께 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-며' ending shows the stammering happening while speaking.

phrases.en: I keep stumbling when I try to speak a foreign language.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 더 흔히 들려요. 말이 막히는 모습에 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and more commonly heard; used for halting speech.

phrases.en: I stutter when I get nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말을 더듬다'는 짝말로 외워 두면 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A handy collocation worth memorizing as a set.

explain_en: Halting speech from nerves or difficulty, neutral to written. Use it when speech doesn't come out smoothly and keeps breaking off or getting stuck. It fits temporary causes such as nervousness, embarrassment or a clumsy foreign language. The similar '더듬거리다' and '말을 더듬다' are also used for this.

t90.ax: I was so nervous that I stammered.

examples.en: The kids are running around noisily and it's chaotic.

examples.ko: 부엌에서는 아침부터 법석법석 음식을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: They've been busily cooking in the kitchen since morning.
The puppy is going wild in front of the door.

examples.ko: 손님이 온다고 법석법석 청소를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: We're cleaning in a flurry because guests are coming.
The market is noisy and bustling with people.

examples.ko: 아침부터 온 가족이 법석법석 짐을 싸고 있어요.
examples.en: The whole family has been packing in a rush since morning.

explain: 시끌시끌 떠들며 바쁘게 움직이는 모습이에요. '북적북적'은 사람이 많아서 붐비는 것에 초점이 있고, '법석법석'은 소란스럽게 움직이는 데 초점이 있어요. 뒤에 '떠들다, 뛰다, 청소하다' 같은 동작이 와요.

phrases.en: The children are making a racket in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시끄럽게 말하고 노는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes noisy talking and playing.

phrases.example: 손님이 온다고 온 가족이 법석법석 청소했어요.
phrases.en: The whole family bustled about cleaning because guests were coming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바쁘게 서두르며 움직이는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a feeling of bustling, hurried movement.

phrases.en: On holiday mornings the house is noisy and lively.
phrases.nuance_ko: '법석법석'처럼 소란스러운 분위기를 나타내지만 움직임보다 소리에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also noisy like 법석법석, but focuses on sound rather than movement.

explain_en: It shows people moving around busily while making a racket. '북적북적' focuses on a place being crowded, whereas '법석법석' focuses on the noisy bustle. Action verbs like '떠들다', '뛰다' and '청소하다' follow it.
